scope: Hypothetical educational case. Preliminary public-information screen only; not regulated advice, a manager interview, operational due diligence or a recommendation to transact.

client.name: Northbridge Education Charity
client.objective: UK CPI + 3% a year after fund costs over rolling five-year periods
client.risk: A fall near 15% triggers trustee review; it is not a loss limit or guarantee
client.liquidity: Daily or weekly dealing; reserve held outside the long-term pool
client.mission: Trustees require explicit look-through review of tobacco, controversial weapons and investments that could conflict with the education mission before appointment

funds.launch: 15 Jun 2018; earlier published history is spliced from the predecessor CIF
funds.eligibility: Eligible UK charities; £10,000 initial and minimum holding
funds.objective: Exceed UK CPI + 4% a year after fees over rolling ten-year periods
funds.liquidity: Daily, 12:00 cut-off; settlement within four business days; large redemptions may be deferred
funds.transaction_cost: 0.13% direct transaction cost for year to 31 Mar 2025
funds.cost_note: Different dates and definitions; the two figures are not a verified all-in cost
funds.risk_indicator: Not machine-readable in the KIID text; visual confirmation required
funds.performance_window: Ten years to 30 Jun 2026; the manager's disclosed target series used RPI to 30 Jun 2018 and CPI thereafter
funds.stress_evidence: -2.9% in the twelve months to 30 Jun 2022; period is not a calendar year
funds.mission: No fund-specific binding tobacco or weapons exclusions identified; firm-level stewardship is not the same as a product screen
funds.governance: Named charity team and a consultative CAIF Advisory Committee; affiliated-fund conflicts still require review
rationales: [C1-C3] Direct real-return objective after fees, but the latest ten-year return was 6.6% versus the manager's 7.9% disclosed target series, which transitions from RPI to CPI and includes predecessor history.
[C1-C3] High equity exposure plus alternatives and possible look-through leverage; no public maximum-drawdown or recovery series.
[C1-C3] Broad asset and manager mix with dynamic allocation, although equities remain the main risk source.
[C1, C4] OCF is below Sarasin's, but transaction and underlying-fund costs need a current reconciliation.
[C2-C5] No binding product-level tobacco or weapons screen was found in the reviewed documents.
[C3, C5] Charity-specific reporting and a CAIF Advisory Committee strengthen oversight, subject to conflict questions.

funds.launch: 23 Feb 2018; earlier published history is spliced from a predecessor fund
funds.eligibility: Eligible UK charities; £1,000 initial and minimum holding
funds.objective: Exceed UK CPI + 4% a year after fees over rolling five-year periods
funds.liquidity: Daily, 11:59 cut-off; normally T+3; large redemptions may be deferred
funds.ocf: 0.94% in the 31 Jul 2026 factsheet; live page and KIID show 0.93%
funds.cost_note: Mechanical sum is about 1.10%, but this is not a verified all-in cost and some closed-ended underlying costs are outside OCF
funds.allocation: 75.2% equities; 13.7% alternatives; 10.2% fixed income; 0.9% liquid assets
funds.mission: Explicit tobacco, weapons, gambling, alcohol and adult-entertainment screens plus stewardship; indirect external funds may not meet every screen
funds.governance: Named multi-asset team and Advisory Committee; the 0.93% and 0.94% public OCF figures require reconciliation
rationales: [S1-S2] The stated CPI + 4% objective matches the case, but five-year net return was 4.85% versus a 9.26% target.
[S1-S3] Risk indicator is 4, but equities and alternatives dominate; 2022 returned -9.8% and maximum drawdown is not public.
[S1-S2] Global multi-asset and thematic process is well described, with look-through liquidity still required for alternatives.
[S1-S3, S6] The highest disclosed cost of the three, with document differences and omitted underlying closed-ended costs.
[S2, S4-S5] The strongest product-level exclusions and stewardship evidence, tempered by incomplete look-through application.
[S2, S6] A named team and committee exist, but the differing public OCF figures should be reconciled before reliance.

funds.launch: 15 Nov 2019 following conversion of the predecessor common investment fund
funds.objective: Outperform a 75% equity / 25% bond composite over five years and deliver at least 3% annual yield
funds.liquidity: Daily, 12:00 cut-off; proceeds normally T+3; exceptional suspension is possible
funds.cost_note: Official 24 Jul 2026 illustration shows total product cost of 0.60%
funds.allocation: Policy range: 60–90% equities; 0–40% bonds and cash; 0–15% other assets. Current factsheet lists 15 holdings but no directly comparable current asset-class table
funds.mission: No product-specific climate-engagement strategy; reviewed public documents do not establish a comprehensive tobacco or controversial-weapons screen
funds.governance: Manager and deputies are named; the fund uses 15 underlying holdings, many affiliated with M&G, so selection and fee conflicts require clarification
rationales: [M1-M2] A 3% yield target supports spending, but the capital-growth target is a market composite rather than CPI + 3%.
[M1-M2] Risk indicator is 4 and calendar 2022 was positive, but one stress period is insufficient: the fund can hold 90% equities and maximum drawdown is not public.
[M1-M2] Flexible multi-asset process, offset by concentration in 15 funds, affiliated products and long-duration gilt exposure.
[M1-M3] Lowest disclosed cost: 0.60% total product cost in the official illustration.
[M2, M4] Product-level mission protections are weak in the reviewed evidence and climate engagement is firm-wide rather than fund-specific.
[M1-M3] Named managers and regular reporting, but affiliated-fund governance and underlying fee rebates need confirmation.

screen_criteria: At least five years of live share-class history
Objective plausibly supports spending and real value
Mission approach is sufficiently explicit for trustee review
Public evidence is sufficient for final appointment

questions.Cazenove: Explain the ten-year 6.6% net return versus the manager's 7.9% disclosed target series, including the RPI-to-CPI transition, predecessor history, allocation and manager-selection attribution.
questions.Sarasin: Explain the five-year 4.85% net return versus 9.26% target and provide supporting performance attribution.
questions.M&G: Explain the five-year 8.16% result versus 8.68% composite and how the 3% yield target affects total return.
questions.decision: Whether the process remains credible after objective misses

questions.Cazenove: Provide monthly net returns, maximum drawdown, recovery time and stress tests for the current legal vehicle.
questions.Sarasin: Provide maximum drawdown, recovery time and downside attribution for 2020, 2022 and the latest stress period.
questions.M&G: Provide maximum drawdown, recovery time and look-through duration/equity stress tests.
questions.decision: Whether a 15% trustee review trigger is workable

questions.Cazenove: Confirm binding product-level exclusions and look-through exposure to tobacco and controversial weapons; distinguish this fund from the sustainable sibling.
questions.Sarasin: Quantify indirect-fund positions outside the screens and provide current controversy and fossil-fuel look-through.
questions.M&G: Confirm product-level tobacco, weapons and coal rules across every underlying fund, including non-M&G holdings.
questions.decision: Whether holdings could conflict with the charity's purposes or reputation

questions.Cazenove: Reconcile current OCF, transaction costs, underlying-fund charges and rebates for a £10m mandate.
questions.Sarasin: Reconcile 0.93% and 0.94% OCF, closed-ended underlying costs, spreads and any dilution levy.
questions.M&G: Confirm the 0.60% total product cost includes the economic effect of every underlying fund and all rebates.
questions.decision: Expected net return available for spending and real-capital preservation

questions.Cazenove: Provide look-through liquidity buckets, property/alternative terms and results of a £10m redemption stress.
questions.Sarasin: Provide look-through liquidity, valuation frequency and notice periods for alternatives and underlying funds.
questions.M&G: Explain liquidity under simultaneous redemptions and long-duration bond stress, including suspension history.
questions.decision: Whether daily dealing remains dependable in stressed markets

questions.Cazenove: Explain affiliated-manager selection, committee independence, team decision rights and succession.
questions.Sarasin: Reconcile the 0.93% and 0.94% public OCF figures and explain committee independence, decision rights and any recent team changes.
questions.M&G: Explain affiliated-fund selection, fee rebates, conflict oversight, decision rights and succession.
questions.decision: Whether trustees can monitor decisions and conflicts

monitoring: Review at least annually; require attribution and a remediation plan after a rolling-horizon target miss
Convene a trustee review near a 15% drawdown; this does not force an automatic sale
Review any lead-manager departure, material turnover or change in decision rights
Review material drift in equity, alternatives, duration, currency or affiliated-fund exposure
Escalate a screen breach, new indirect exposure or weaker exclusion policy
Review any OCF rise, new performance fee or unreconciled underlying cost
Review any redemption deferral, suspension or deterioration in look-through liquidity
Escalate unresolved disclosure discrepancies or delayed risk and holdings reporting
